articles.title: Educative’s Journey From Grokking System Design to Grokking Modern System Design
articles.excerpt: When we started building interview preparation at Educative, the goal was never to predict every question a developer might encounter. I was more interested in making difficult interviews feel less ar…
articles.body: When we started building interview preparation at Educative, the goal was never to predict every question a developer might encounter. I was more interested in making difficult interviews feel less arbitrary. System Design was a perfect example: strong engineers could understand databases, caches, queues, and distributed systems individually, yet still find it difficult to turn those pieces into a coherent architecture when somebody handed them an ambiguous problem. That challenge became an important part of Educative’s Grokking journey. Over time, though, the interview surface around it grew much larger. The fundamentals remained useful, but the jobs developers were preparing for, and the systems those jobs involved, kept expanding.

articles.title: I almost translated my product. The demand was 90.6% English, and most of it wasn't from English-speaking countries
articles.excerpt: I had localisation on the roadmap. Italian first, since that's where I am and where a visible share of my traffic came from, then a couple of others. I measured before building. 90.6% of the demand wa…
articles.body: I had localisation on the roadmap. Italian first, since that's where I am and where a visible share of my traffic came from, then a couple of others. I measured before building. 90.6% of the demand was in English. Including a large share of the demand coming from countries where English isn't the first language. The project got cancelled. Here's the measurement, because the mistake I nearly made is built into the default shape of every analytics dashboard. Country is not language Every analytics tool leads with geography. Sessions by country, top countries, a map. It's the easiest dimension to collect — one IP lookup — so it's the one that's front and centre. And it quietly answers a different question than the one you're asking.

articles.title: New Magic Leak Confirms Fully-Foil Spider-Man Commander Deck
articles.excerpt: A new leak seems to confirm that Marvel's Spider-Man will finally get an MTG Commander deck this Christmas.
articles.body: Marvel's Spider-Man is a Magic: The Gathering Universes Beyond set that came out in September 2025. Notably, the set lacked preconstructed Commander decks, a popular product for fans of Magic 's multiplayer variant. Magic 's head designer Mark Rosewater explained that Marvel's Spider-Man began its design cycle as a very small set, but then Wizards of the Coast decided to expand it. However, there wasn't a lot of time for the pivot, so Commander decks were left on the cutting-room floor. Still, Rosewater also added that the product could appear in the future, a claim that seemed confirmed this past June by a leak , and now sees further support from new, unofficial information.

articles.excerpt: Samsung's latest smartwatch is better, faster, and frustratingly familiar.
articles.body: I’ve been wearing a Galaxy Watch 7 for two years. Samsung threw trade-in offers at me throughout the Watch 8 cycle, and I didn’t bite, partly because I was between jobs at the time and partly because my Watch 7 was still doing everything I needed. So when the Galaxy Watch 9 () showed up, I was ready to be impressed. Two generations is a long time to sit out. Whatever Samsung had been cooking for its new smartwatches , I was going to feel all of it at once. But after three weeks of using it, I’ve realized that while the Galaxy Watch 9 is a very good smartwatch, it’s not one I can wholeheartedly recommend without one very familiar asterisk.

articles.excerpt: Pixels are still sleeping through their own alarms, and so is Google.
articles.body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Some Pixel owners are still struggling with a long-standing bug that prevents alarms from going off. All they get is a notification that says “alarm didn’t fire for an unknown reason.” The issue has been around since at least 2021, and Google previously promised to fix it, though it seems that’s not the case. Google Pixel phones have a long-standing bug with the Clock app that prevents alarms from going off on time. It has hampered users’ experience for years now, and we can trace reports back to as early as 2021 . While Google claimed to have fixed it, newer reports keep cropping up every now and then, and that hasn’t changed. We’ve spotted newer reports coming from Pixel users about the alarm not firing when intended.

articles.title: 20 Years Later, the Most Inventive Sci-Fi Superhero Series of the Century is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.excerpt: There's been no better time to revisit one of the best superhero shows ever made.
articles.body: Superhero television used to be way weirder. Before Marvel and DC 's blockbuster cinematic universes streamlined the cape-and-cowl blueprint, TV was a wild west for superpower narratives rooted in human drama rather than comic book lore. The 4400 treated sudden gifts as a sprawling sci-fi mystery, while Syfy’s Alphas reinterpreted abilities as complex neurological conditions with severe real-world trade-offs. Even modern juggernauts like The Boys thrive on this subversive DNA, turning superpowered individuals into cynical corporate commodities and uncontrollable liability risks.
articles.author: Ryan Epps

articles.body: The Bear’s Ebon Moss-Bachrach is reportedly in final talks to join Michael Mann’s Heat 2 as Kelso, according to TheWrap . Kelso is the mysterious former DARPA researcher and hacker who furnishes Neil McCauley character with the intel he needs to take down his scores. Kelso was played by Tom Noonan in the 1995 original. Noonan passed away earlier this year, in February . The two-time Emmy winner will join a stacked cast, including Leonardo DiCaprio as Chris Shiherlis (originally played by Val Kilmer), Christian Bale as Detective Vincent Hanna (originally played by Al Pacino), and Stephen Graham in Robert De Niro’s old role as Neil McCauley. Shooting is reportedly scheduled to begin in November.

articles.title: NASA Welcomes Côte d’Ivoire as Newest Artemis Accords Signatory
articles.excerpt: Côte d’Ivoire signed the Artemis Accords on Thursday, becoming the 75th signatory and marking a major milestone for this growing coalition. With the signing ceremony in the nation’s largest city, Abid…
articles.body: Credit: NASA Côte d’Ivoire signed the Artemis Accords on Thursday, becoming the 75th signatory and marking a major milestone for this growing coalition. With the signing ceremony in the nation’s largest city, Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire joined other like-minded nations and committed to the peaceful, transparent, and responsible exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. “The United States and Côte d’Ivoire already cooperate on Earth,” said NASA’s Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. “Today, we expand that partnership beyond it. Joining the Artemis Accords opens new opportunities for our scientists, engineers, and institutions to work together as humanity returns to the Moon and prepares for what comes next. We’ve aligned on the principles. The opportunities are in front of us.

articles.body: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA announced the winners of the Deep Space Food Challenge: Mars to Table Thursday, with the top $300,000 prize being awarded to Chinyere Ukeje of Philadelphia, Pa. for the Adaptive Nourishment Infrastructure (ANI) food system concept. This competition challenged solvers to explore innovative solutions for integrated space food systems that would provide safe, nutritious meals to astronauts living and working in space.    Mars to Table launched in January 2026 as a follow on to the Deep Space Food Challenge , which NASA ran from 2021-2014 in collaboration with CSA (Canadian Space Agency).

articles.title: NASA’s Machines for Mars Make Beer Bubbly
articles.excerpt: Carbon-capture technology repurposed for breweries spreads and finds new applications
articles.body: 3 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) A brewer makes adjustments to the Earthly Labs carbon-capture unit, which purifies carbon dioxide from the beer brewing process for use in carbonation. Credit: Chart Industries Inc. In 2021, Maine Beer Company’s carbon dioxide supplier ran short on carbon dioxide. “There was potential for our beer to go stale in the tanks,” said Dave Love, the brewery’s sustainability manager. “We wouldn’t be able to use CO 2   for any of our bottling, kegging, or centrifuge operations.” The solution the company settled on originated on Mars — or more specifically, in NASA’s plans for harvesting resources from the Red Planet.
